Hi Camila — thanks for the recap. Attaching the request dump and stack trace (request_dump.json, finlytics_stacktrace.txt). We started getting 500s hitting your embeddings endpoint while running a nightly scoring job. Details below: 

- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
- SDK: redwood-js v0.9.1 (we used the batchEmbeddings helper)
- Payload size: ~120 documents, ~50 tokens avg
- Error: intermittent 500/502 and a couple of 504 timeouts. Attached stack trace shows a 500 inside the server handler at 2026-03-01T15:47:21Z.

We tried increasing our client timeout to 60s with no consistent improvement. The reranker flow calls embeddings first then a separate reranker model endpoint — the failures appear during the embedding batch step.

Any immediate recommendations? If Dev can repro, happy to schedule a short debug session.

Thanks,
Tom Harris
Senior ML Engineer | FinLytics
tharris@finlytics.com

Thanks for the ping — I dug into the request dump and stacktrace. Quick summary and repro guidance below.

Findings:
- The payload shows large batch size (~120) and a single POST that produces a large memory working set on the inference node. In hosted mode we've seen this trigger transient 5xxs when the node is near memory pressure.
- stacktrace suggests an internal OOM path that surfaces as a 500; couple of 502/504s are proxied timeouts.
- SDK v0.9.1 uses a JSON batch helper that sends entire batch in one request by default — recommend batching client-side.

Immediate recommendations (to share with FinLytics):
1) Reduce embedding batch size to 16 (or 32) as a quick mitigation.
2) Add exponential backoff with jitter on 500/502/504 responses.
3) Increase client timeout to 120s for large jobs while we triage.
4) If using private/dedicated deployment: confirm node GPU memory + kernel selection; there are known edge cases with quantized kernels for very long sequences.

Repro steps (what I ran locally):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @request_dump.json

I reproduced a 500 locally when sending the full 120-item payload. Retrying with --data-binary of a 16-item subset succeeded.

Action items from infra side:
- I filed INF-1123 to add better request-size guarding and clearer 413-like errors instead of 500s for oversized batches.
- Short term: we can enable request-level queueing for this customer if they expect large nightly jobs.

Let me know if you want me to join a screen share with FinLytics.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Dev — thanks for the quick triage, that aligns with what we suspected. I ran the smaller-batch test and the 500s stopped. A couple of follow-ups: 

- What do you recommend for embedding+reranker latency budgets? We need to set sensible client timeouts. For nightly scoring (not user-facing) 120s is acceptable, but for online inference we'll need <1s end-to-end.
- Any recommended config for the reranker call (we do embeddings -> reranker with ~200 candidates)?

Also, can you confirm if we should be using streaming or chunked requests for long runs?

Happy to jump on a short call — otherwise we’ll implement batch=16 and backoff and report back.

Thanks,
Tom
